items.definition:
to cause (a great deal of damage or harm)
The storm threatened to wreak havoc on the coastal towns.

to cause a loss of dignity or respect for (someone or something)
His rude comments demeaned the entire team.

to make known (private information)
He refused to divulge the source of his information.

to raise a design on a surface
The leather cover was embossed with the company's logo.

to expose to radiation; to illuminate
Scientists can irradiate food to kill bacteria.

To confirm or give support to (a statement, theory, or finding).
The witness's testimony helped to corroborate the suspect's alibi.

to name
The currency is denominated in euros.

to clear from blame
The DNA evidence helped to exonerate the suspect.

to make pregnant; to saturate
The fabric was impregnated with a waterproof coating.

to measure the depth of (water); to explore or examine deeply
The detective tried to plumb the depths of the suspect's mind.

To decorate with small, sparkling objects
The night sky was spangled with stars.

To place or lay (one thing) over another so that both are still discernible
The artist decided to superimpose a new image onto the existing background.

enclose (something) in or as if in a capsule; express the essential features of (something) succinctly
The report aims to encapsulate the main findings of the research.

to inspire or permeate with a feeling or quality
His art is imbued with a sense of peace and tranquility.

to represent (an abstract quality or idea) as a person or thing
She seemed to personify grace and elegance.

to exist before something else
Some believe that souls preexist their physical bodies.

to represent inadequately
The survey results might underrepresent the opinions of younger voters.

to defeat thoroughly
The knight set out to vanquish the dragon.

to distress or treat unfairly
The company's decision to cut benefits aggrieved many employees.

to deprive of a loved one through a profound absence, especially due to death
The war had bereaved many families of their sons.

To destroy (oneself or something) deliberately.
The missile was programmed to destruct if it went off course.

To deprive (someone) of the right to vote.
Laws were passed to prevent attempts to disenfranchise minority voters.

adopt or support (a cause, belief, or way of life)
She decided to espouse the cause of environmental protection.

to inspire someone with an intense but short-lived passion or admiration
He was infatuated with her beauty.

to remove the foreskin
In some cultures, it is traditional to circumcise male infants.

to move with a smooth, wavelike motion
The fields of wheat undulated in the gentle breeze.

to release from restraints or limitations; to free
The new policies aim to unfetter economic growth.

to make receptive or aware; to bring into harmony
It takes time to attune yourself to a new culture.

to regard or represent as being of little worth
It's wrong to disparage someone's efforts, even if they fail.

to strip or deprive (someone or something) of power, rights, or possessions
The company decided to divest its holdings in fossil fuels.

to send or deliver
He decided to consign his old furniture to an auction house.

engage in dishonest and fraudulent business dealings
The gang tried to racketeer by extorting money from local businesses.

be filled with intense but unexpressed anger
He was seething with rage after the unfair decision.

to make amends or reparation
He tried to atone for his mistakes by helping others.

to formally engage to be married
They were betrothed at a young age.

to make (attitudes or behavior) part of one's nature by learning or unconscious assimilation
It takes time to internalize new concepts.

Form (an idea or opinion) in advance.
It's important not to preconceive ideas about people before you meet them.

to cover (a roof or a building) with straw or similar material
They decided to thatch the roof of their new cottage.

split or sever (something), especially along a natural line or grain
The axe was used to cleave the log in two.

To make legally null and void; invalidate
The judge decided to nullify the contract due to fraud.

To annoy or irritate.
The constant noise began to vex him.

take out of service
The old power plant will be decommissioned next year.

beg someone earnestly or desperately to do something
She implored him to reconsider his decision.

to provide evidence to support or prove the truth of
You need to substantiate your claims with facts.

to grow teeth
The baby is starting to teethe, which makes him a bit fussy.

to surprise or confuse someone; to prove (a theory, expectation, or prediction) wrong
The sudden turn of events confounded everyone.

to separate and go in different directions
The two paths diverge at the old oak tree.

to take possession of a mortgaged property when the mortgagor fails to keep up their mortgage payments
The bank threatened to foreclose on their house.

to make something a political issue
The media quickly politicized the debate, causing it to lose its original focus.

build up again from parts; restore to liquid form
You need to add water to reconstitute the dried soup.

be born again in another body
Some religions believe that souls can reincarnate after death.

to form or create a jagged, saw-like edge
The machine serrated the edge of the blade.

charge with an additional amount of power or energy
The new technology will supercharge the company's growth.

intrude on (a person's territory or a thing considered to be a right).
The sea has started to encroach on the coastline.

officially exclude (someone) from participation in the sacraments and services of the Christian Church.
The bishop threatened to excommunicate the rebellious priest.

weave together or entwine
The author skillfully interwove several plotlines into a single narrative.

to wound or injure (someone) so that part of the body is permanently damaged
The accident left him maimed for life.

to involve (someone or something) in a difficult or unpleasant situation
The company was mired in debt after the failed investment.

To make someone liable or inclined to a specified attitude, action, or condition
Genetic factors can predispose individuals to certain diseases.

To designate again or differently
The committee decided to redesignate the old building as a historical landmark.

To support (an organization or activity) financially
The government decided to subsidise public transport.

To supersede and replace
New technology will soon supplant older methods.

to hand over a person to another jurisdiction
The government decided to extradite the suspect.

suggest or assume the existence of
Scientists postulate the existence of dark matter.
